$description: Carries a paper base and a full ink restatement: this one theme answers to both modes.

color.$description: Two greys and a red. The light mode is paper; the dark mode is ink; the ramp carries both, mirrored, untinted, so nothing competes with the red.

primary.$description: The widow red itself: primary actions, links, focus rings. Deep enough to hold white text at 4.5:1.

secondary.$description: The ink block: a solid near-black control on paper, the poster's second voice.

accent.$description: The lit red: same thread, one read brighter, for emphasis that should feel like it is on.

neutral.$description: The ink ramp, 50 (paper end) through 900 (ink end). Zero chroma on purpose: a widow grey is a grey, never a guest hue, so the red stands alone at full strength.

semantic.$description: Status colors. Named by meaning, never by hue — on a red brand, danger slices itself narrower than the primary so the two reds never read as one.

surface.$description: The page. Paper in the light mode; the ramp carries the ink page in the dark one.

surface-sunken.$description: Background of elements that sit below the page: table stripes, inset wells.

surface-raised.$description: Background of elements that sit above the page: cards, popovers, menus. Pure white on the paper page; on ink, one clean step up in the same language.

text.$description: Body text: ink on paper, paper on ink.

text-muted.$description: Secondary text: captions, helper copy, placeholders.

border.$description: The hairline. A widow draws in thread: one-pixel strokes, stronger here than in softer themes, because the sheet is held together by its lines.

scrim.$description: What dims the page behind a modal — the theme's own ink.

link.$description: The red thread through running text: a link is the widow red, no underline of another color.

field.$description: A field's own surface: white on paper, a lifted step on ink. — a control reads as an object set on the page, not a hole punched through it.

border-strong.$description: A control's own edge — the thread drawn tighter. Stronger than `border`, which divides content.

on-semantic-error.$description: Text on the matching fill. A fill with no foreground cannot be read, which is what this token prevents.

spacing.$description: The spacing scale. Every gap, pad and inset is one of these steps.

font.$description: Typography: a didone speaks, the grotesk works, the mono is code. The display face is the brand's voice; the working faces stay quiet so it carries.

sans.$description: Body and UI text: the working voice, quiet and even.

heading.$value: Bodoni Moda, Didot, "Bodoni MT", "Times New Roman", serif
heading.$description: The display voice. A didone: hairline serifs, strong stems, all menace and poise — the widow red's natural partner.

body.$description: The body face: the sans, named so the surface is whole.

serif.$description: Long-form editorial text. The didone is too sharp to read for pages; the editorial voice stays a book serif.

brand.$description: The logotype face — one brand, every starter.

size.$description: The display end reaches further than most themes dare: a didone is measured in headlines, not paragraphs.

letter-spacing.$description: How far the letters sit from each other. A didone is spaced open where the hairlines need air and closed nowhere.

tighter.$description: Display type only. A didone carries its own tension; a theme never pinches it.

wide.$description: The small uppercase label, spun into thread.

wider.$description: An eyebrow or category mark above the copy it introduces.

widest.$description: A single word carrying a whole section. Poster spacing.

radius.$description: Corner rounding, barely there: a thread ends blunt, and sharp corners are the poster's geometry.

0.$description: Gone, not merely faint. The step a rule reaches for when the element should not be painted at all.

10.$description: A ghost: present in the DOM, gone from the eye. Reserved for decoration.

20.$description: Disabled. Low enough to stop a control being pressed, high enough to keep its label readable beside live controls.

30.$description: A disabled control on a dark surface, where the same fraction reads lighter than it does on a light one.

40.$description: The dimmed step: a placeholder image, a track before it is filled, a hint of content.

50.$description: Half. The step most rules ask for, so it is the one a theme is most likely to have an opinion about.

60.$description: Muted but still read: text on a disabled field that the reader is expected to transcribe.

70.$description: Secondary content that must survive a projector or a bright room.

80.$description: A hair under full strength: the hover state of something that should feel nearly solid.

90.$description: Almost opaque. The step for a scrim that must dim what is behind it without appearing to.

100.$description: Fully shown. The default, named so a rule can say it rather than assume it.

opacity.$description: How much of a thing is shown, as a fraction. A theme owns this because the same fraction reads differently over a light surface than over a dark one, and because `disabled` is a decision about how present a dead control still looks.

shadow.$description: Elevation, as CSS box-shadow values. A widow separates with line, not with light; shadows stay small and drop straight down.

breakpoint.$description: Viewport widths where layout steps change.

z-index.$description: Stacking order. Layer, never a magic number at the call site.

motion.$description: How things move and how long it takes. The widow is quick: a spider responds, it does not glide.

button.$description: Character: the decisions a theme owns for its buttons. The widow's button is a small poster — uppercase, tracked open, flat — drawn rather than lit.

weight.$description: The button's own weight. A control carries more weight than the prose around it.

case.$description: Labels are set in capitals: the poster voice, even in a control.

tracking.$description: Label tracking. Open, because uppercase 600 needs the air to read as words rather than a wall.

shadow.$description: The resting elevation: a whisper of drop, no lit pedestal.

shadow-hover.$description: The hovered elevation: the thread catches light. Red, not black — a button does not grow darker when it wakes.

border.$description: Stroke weight. Every control and surface reads `width`, so a theme changes its edge weight in one place; the numbered steps above it are the ladder a layout reaches for when one edge needs to say more than the rest.

width.$description: The hairline every control and surface draws with — the thread itself.

width-2.$description: The emphasis edge: a control that must read as selected rather than merely bordered.

width-4.$description: The heavy edge. Rare on purpose — a stroke this thick is a statement, not a divider.

width-8.$description: The frame. A block drawn rather than outlined.

focus.$description: The focus ring, shared by every interactive element: buttons, links, fields, summaries and dialogs.

width.$description: The ring's stroke. Two pixels in both modes: a one-pixel ring reads as a rendering artifact rather than a decision.

icon.$description: Glyph sizes, from the reader's own root rather than the element they sit in — a step has to be a jump, and an `em` step against 14px prose is 2px.

badge.$description: Character: the decisions a theme owns for its badges. The widow's badge is a square tag with an edge drawn like thread — no pills.

edge.$description: The stroke the badge draws around itself, so a small shape holds apart from the page.

pill.$description: A pill is a soft word. The widow squares its badges into tags.

checkbox.$description: How physical a checkbox is: one scalar driving three inset shadows. Zero is flat and drawn — the widow's controls are drawn, not lit.

switch.$description: How physical a switch is: one scalar driving three inset shadows. Zero is flat and drawn; higher is lit and raised.

avatar.$description: How big an avatar is, as the edge of the square it fills. A theme owns the ladder because the size of a face is a design decision, not a product of some other token.

sm.$description: The size for a face in a list or a comment: it reads beside its label without leading the row.

md.$description: The default: a face beside a name, or a profile header at rest.

lg.$description: A face as the subject of a page: a profile header at the top of a long column.
